topic: Native vs React Native vs Flutter for founders
caption:
Native, React Native or Flutter? It's one of the first questions every app founder asks, and the answer is less about technology than you'd think. 📱

Swipe through for the founder's version:

✅ Native when your app lives on the hardware (camera, Bluetooth, heavy background work)
✅ Cross-platform when you need iOS + Android fast on one budget, which covers most business apps
✅ Decide on your roadmap and who will maintain it, not on hype

Not sure which fits your idea? DM us the word STACK with a one-line description and we'll tell you what we'd pick and why. Free.

Save this for when you start your app. 🔖

slides.title: Native, React Native or Flutter: which does your app need?
slides.sub: The honest answer depends on three things. Swipe →

cols.name: Native
cols.text: Best performance and deepest device access. Two codebases, so a higher build and maintenance cost.

cols.name: React Native
cols.text: One codebase for iOS and Android, huge ecosystem. A strong fit for most business apps.

cols.name: Flutter
cols.text: One codebase with a pixel-consistent UI. A smaller hiring pool than JavaScript.

slides.title: Choose native when…
slides.body: your app lives on the hardware: heavy camera or AR work, Bluetooth devices, complex background tasks, or high-end games.

slides.title: Choose cross-platform when…
slides.body: you need iOS and Android fast, on one budget, and your app is mostly screens, forms, maps, payments and real-time updates. That's most startups.

slides.title: Don't decide on hype.
slides.body: Decide on your roadmap, your budget and who will maintain the app two years from now.
